newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch try to end EU split on farm revaluation aid.
newsitem.headline: Dutch try to end EU split on farm revaluation aid.

text.p: The Dutch Presidency of the European Union will on Wednesday try to end a split among farm ministers over a plan to limit farmers' compensation for income loss due to a major currency revaluation, an EU diplomat said.
Three countries, Britain, Ireland and Italy, have blocked a European Commission proposal to limit the amount of compensation that farmers could receive.

The three countries currencies have recently undergone a series of revaluations and the Commission estimates that compensation under existing rules would cost 1.8 billion ecus in 1998 and following years.
The three countries say that the measure would be discriminatory because it did not apply to Germany, the Netherlands and six other countries which revalued in the past.
"The Commission told ministers that it was not discriminatory but a council legal opinion suggested that it could be," the diplomat said.
A spokesman for the Dutch presidency said that a revised proposal, that would not be discriminatory, would be presented on Wednesday.
